doc.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26

title: Meeting King Baldwin and moving to New Orleans at 21
summary: Ory stays in Laplace until 21, is heard by a bandleader who invites him to play, and leaves the morning he turns 21.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: How old were you when you moved to New Orleans? I was always wondering...
Oh, I was 21. I had to stay there until I was 21. But I used to visit them all then.
Used to visit. But you waited for about 21 to move down. Yeah.

And when I bought my first goods out from Baltimore... paid $65 that I was blowing at my sister's house. And the bull didn't happen to be passing on the sidewalk and he heard it. And I'm going to go and say... Oh, you the young man blowing that horn? Yeah. And the young man trying to blow it. He said, well, you sound good. He said, I'm the king.
I said, King who is there? King Baldwin. Oh, I said, how are you, Mr. Baldwin, King?

He said, would you like to play with me? I said, very much so. I said, wait a minute. I ran back in the kitchen in the sister's back. I said, oh, that one made a wife. And boy, I was so happy. He said, no, you have to go back home and go to school. You promised your dad he was on the staff there in the 21. And when it was 21, 4 o'clock in the morning and 8 o'clock I was on the train. I've been gone ever since. Well, I was playing professionally, playing dances, you know. Oh, yeah, sure. That was about 18 then. About 18-4 then, huh? Yeah. And when it was 21, 4 o'clock in the morning, and 8 o'clock I was on the train. I've been gone ever since.
How old were you, Ren Bold, and heard you?
Well, I was about 18 then. Well, I was playing professionally, playing dances, you know.
Oh, yeah, sure. That was about 18-4 then, huh?
